reviewed_arguments: H0--H1 retain arbitrary manifolds, all permitted generalized continuations, every full target remainder, original Banach trace hypotheses and one uniform parameter neighborhood before target orders.

D0--D3 normalize failure of finite lists, prove all fixed-column square sums, retain one output neighborhood at all orders and produce a relatively closed characteristic target defect disjoint from the observation cone.

P0 retains both characteristic roots, every full incoming window and every local propagation regime. Only the reduced witness has the first-order expansion: x=O(t^2), xi=O(t), kappa=O(t^3) justify its smooth compressed-coordinate transformation. Normal roots use the separate signed-root joining theorem.

P1 handles stationary exceptions and dimension one explicitly. A one-dimensional interior characteristic has radial or zero Hamilton field; the boundary has no nonzero tangential compressed characteristic. Global closed-defect continuation contradicts the exact compact-access theorem.

S0 yields actual one-source/one-observation estimates for noncompact boundaries, dimension one, no boundary and separately suitable compact channels. Parameter ranges are not shrunk by these post-selection scalar constructions.

T0 proves the actual finite-tested completion by full transposes and uniform target-family limits. It assumes no density in a larger maximal graph; T1 keeps the restricted-cone compact scalar case and all other course obligations active.

The three solutions check signed periodic-cylinder access times, a compact two-boundary billiard using two different scalar assemblies, an admissible continuous Banach trace space, and the exact derivative-graph density obstruction.
